escena: SCENE (Efeonce office, Santiago, high floor, late morning): the back wall of the Efeonce meeting room «Responder.», seen from the chair of someone sitting at the meeting table — camera at SEATED EYE LEVEL (about 1.15 m), 28 mm lens at f/5.6, like a good webcam view, looking straight at a matte dark-navy wall 2.5 m away; horizon level, verticals straight. LEFT THIRD: the Efeonce logo from Image 1 mounted high on the navy wall as dimensional signage about 0.8 m wide, the WHOLE logo inside the LEFT 28% of the frame width (from about 5% to 28%) and between 10% and 28% of the frame height, so a person sitting in the centre never covers any part of it: satin white acrylic letters and emblem standing 4 cm off the wall on hidden pins, with a soft cool-white LED halo glowing on the wall behind every letter, so it reads as a real backlit sign whose glow fades into the dark wall. RIGHT THIRD: Image 2 is the final artwork of that part of the wall — the room name «Responder» in white letters with its sphere as the period and, under it, a tall portrait whiteboard with the handwritten question, a small handwritten header, the three handwritten tool names and their tally marks. Reproduce Image 2 exactly as real materials: the room name is cut matte white vinyl lettering applied flat on the wall and the sphere an azure vinyl dot; the whiteboard is a real glossy enamel board with an aluminium frame and a marker tray, the writing real dry-erase marker ink with slightly uneven strokes. At the far RIGHT edge a narrow strip of floor-to-ceiling glass shows the bright open office beyond, out of focus: pale oak desks, a current-generation borderless monitor with a blue screen glow, tall windows with the Andes far away. LIGHT: hard, low late-morning sunlight enters from that right edge, crossing the right third as crisp visible shafts through the haze and raking across the room name and the whiteboard with sharp window-mullion shadows; the centre of the wall stays in calm, even shade; on the left only the logo's own LED halo lights the wall. TRACES OF WORK: a black dry-erase marker with its cap off lying on the whiteboard tray; a mesh office chair pushed back at an angle below the whiteboard; at the bottom right corner the blurred near edge of the oak meeting table with a current-generation thin laptop half-open, its screen dark. Nothing else on the walls: no books, no plants, no posters, no clocks, no extra signage and no extra text anywhere. TEXT EXCEPTION: the logo from Image 1 and the artwork from Image 2 are the ONLY readable marks in the picture; they stay crisp and fully legible, every letter, word and tally mark exactly as in the references, never blurred, altered or translated; every other screen or paper stays illegible by physical means.
